statement: The historical and adopted localizer axioms are different formulations. The literal Loc~(1) of XVI ms.~1 consists of isomorphisms, two-out-of-three, and the condition that $gf,fg\in W$ imply $f,g\in W$. Grothendieck calls the first two conditions \emph{saturation faible}, and all three \emph{saturation mod\'er\'ee}. Retract closure is added in Loc~(1 bis); strong saturation is Loc~(1 ter). The literal Loc~(3), XVI ms.~2, is absolute Theorem~A. Relative Theorem~A is Loc~(3 bis), ms.~3. In this paper, a fundamental localizer means the modern relative package specified in the conventions: weak saturation, the terminal-object axiom, and the assertion that a functor $u:A\to B$ over $C$ lies in $W$ whenever $u/c:A/c\to B/c$ lies in $W$ for every $c\in C$. Consequently no argument using relative Theorem~A is an argument from the literal absolute Loc~(3) alone.
title: Historical versus adopted localizer axioms

statement: Intrinsic fibrations and their unconditional closure properties. Let $\mathcal M$ have pullbacks and let $W$ be invariant under isomorphism of arrows. For $S\in\mathcal M$, let $W_S$ be the inverse image of $W$ under the source functor $\mathcal M/S\to\mathcal M$. Define \[ \operatorname{Fib}_W=\{p:E\to B\mid p^*: \mathcal M/B\to\mathcal M/E\text{ sends }W_B\text{ into }W_E\}. \] Thus every test is an arrow $v:T'\to T$ over $B$, with arbitrary structure map $T\to B$, and the tested arrow is $E\times_B T'\to E\times_B T$. This class contains isomorphisms and is closed under composition and arbitrary pullback. These assertions require no two-out-of-three axiom. If $W$ is closed under retracts, then so is $\operatorname{Fib}_W$.

statement: The coarse, universal, and local relative classes. Suppose $W$ contains isomorphisms and satisfies two-out-of-three. Let $\mathcal L$ contain isomorphisms and be closed under composition and pullback. For an arrow $u:X\to Y$ in $\mathcal M/S$, put \[ u\in W_S^{\mathcal L}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \bigl(X\times_S T\longrightarrow Y\times_S T\bigr)\in W \quad\hbox{for every }(T\to S)\in\mathcal L. \] Let $W_S^u$ be the same class with all $T\to S$ allowed. Then \[ W_S^u\subseteq W_S^{\mathcal L}\subseteq W_S. \] All three classes contain isomorphisms and satisfy two-out-of-three. Their retract closure follows if $W$ has it. These are precisely the relative classes in XII ms.~210 and 220. They must not be confused with the class of universal $W$-equivalences in $\mathcal M$, where the base is the codomain of the arrow being tested.

statement: What raw reindexing and postcomposition actually preserve. Under the hypotheses of A.3, a map $f:S'\to S$ in $\mathcal L$ induces \[ f^*:(\mathcal M/S,W_S^{\mathcal L})\longrightarrow (\mathcal M/S',W_{S'}^{\mathcal L}). \] For every $f:S'\to S$, without assuming $f\in\mathcal L$, postcomposition induces \[ f_\#:(\mathcal M/S',W_{S'}^{\mathcal L})\longrightarrow (\mathcal M/S,W_S^{\mathcal L}). \] If $f^*$ also preserves the displayed classes, the ordinary adjunction $f_\#\dashv f^*$ descends to their localizations. For arbitrary $f$, this calculation alone constructs the descended postcomposition functor; it does not construct its right adjoint.

statement: The universal saturation of the local test class. Moreover \[ W_S^{\widehat{\mathcal L}}=W_S^{\mathcal L} \quad\hbox{for every }S,\qquad \widehat{\widehat{\mathcal L}}=\widehat{\mathcal L}. \] It is the largest composition- and pullback-closed class containing isomorphisms that defines this same family of fine relative classes. statement: The corrected transporter Galois connection. Let $W$ contain isomorphisms and be closed under composition in a category $\mathcal M$ with pullbacks. Let $A\subseteq W$ contain isomorphisms and be composition-closed, and let $L$ contain isomorphisms and be pullback-closed. Define \[ \begin{split} T_W(A)&=\{p:E\to B\mid p^*\text{ sends every arrow of }A \text{ in }\mathcal M/B\text{ into }W\},\\ K_W(L)&=\{u:X\to Y\in W\mid p^*u\in W \text{ for every }(p:Y'\to Y)\in L\}. \end{split} \] Then $T_W(A)$ contains isomorphisms and is pullback-closed, $K_W(L)$ contains isomorphisms and is composition-closed, and \[ A\subseteq K_W(L)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad L\subseteq T_W(A). \] Both operations reverse inclusions; their composites are extensive, monotone, and idempotent. The closed pairs are exchanged by inverse order-reversing bijections. Their extreme pairs are \[ (W^u,\operatorname{Mor}\mathcal M),\qquad (W,\operatorname{Fib}_W), \] where $W^u$ means universal equivalences with respect to the codomain of each arrow.

statement: The meaning of smooth and proper in the manuscript. statement: The four fibration classes and Loc (7), with reference localizer. For a fundamental localizer $W$, the four classes in XVI section~4 are distinct definitions. Besides intrinsic $\operatorname{Fib}_W$, one has Grothendieck fibrations; $\operatorname{Fib}^{\mathrm{weak}}_W$, tested by all arrows $T'\to T$ over the base with $T'$ and $T$ contractible in the category-homotopy sense; and $\operatorname{Parf}_W=\operatorname{Liss}_W\cap\operatorname{Prop}_W$. Here category-homotopy contractibility means that the identity functor is connected to a constant functor by a finite zigzag of natural transformations. It implies weak contractibility of the nerve, but replacing the test family by all weakly contractible nerves is a separate assertion, not the literal definition. Let $\mathcal G_W$ denote Grothendieck fibrations all of whose transport functors lie in $W$. For any arrow class $\mathcal F$, define \[ \begin{aligned} \mathrm A(\mathcal F)&:\quad\mathcal F\subseteq\operatorname{Fib}_W,\\ \mathrm B(\mathcal F)&:\quad W_S\cap\operatorname{Mor}(\mathcal F/S) \subseteq W_S^u\quad\hbox{for every }S,\\ \mathrm C(\mathcal F)&:\quad\mathcal F\cap W\subseteq W^u. \end{aligned} \] Loc~(7a), (7b), and (7c) are respectively $\mathrm A(\mathcal G_W)$, $\mathrm B(\mathcal G_W)$, and $\mathrm C(\mathcal G_W)$. For a reference localizer $V\subseteq W$, the conditions $\mathrm A_V,\mathrm B_V,\mathrm C_V$ replace $\mathcal G_W$ by $\mathcal G_V$. The condition $\mathrm D_V$ is $\mathrm A(\operatorname{Parf}_V)$, or its equivalent B and C forms once the hypotheses of A.17 are verified. Loc~(7F) is the factorization condition of A.11, not the inclusion of any one of these reference classes in $\operatorname{Fib}_W$.

statement: The implications A to B to C and replacement transfer. Let $W$ and $\mathcal M$ satisfy A.11's initial assumptions. If every map factors as a $W$-map followed by a member of $\mathcal F$, then $\mathrm A(\mathcal F)$ implies $\mathrm B(\mathcal F)$. If identities lie in $\mathcal F$, then $\mathrm B(\mathcal F)$ implies $\mathrm C(\mathcal F)$. Suppose that each $p:X\to S$ in $\mathcal F$ admits a comparison $j_p:X\to R_p$ over $S$ in $W_S^u$, with $R_p\to S$ in $\mathcal G$. Then $\mathrm A(\mathcal G)\Rightarrow\mathrm A(\mathcal F)$ and $\mathrm C(\mathcal G)\Rightarrow\mathrm C(\mathcal F)$. If for every map $h:X\to Y$ over $S$ between $\mathcal F$-objects the chosen comparisons extend to a commutative square $R(h)j_X=j_Yh$, then also $\mathrm B(\mathcal G)\Rightarrow\mathrm B(\mathcal F)$. Functorial replacements suffice; the proof only needs these individual commuting squares.

statement: The local-coefficient repair has an asymmetric conclusion. Let $\mathbb D$ be a derivator in presheaf variance. Suppose that for $p:E\to B$, after every strict base change, the right direct image of every constant coefficient is locally constant and its value at each base object is canonically the right Kan extension from the strict fibre. If $v:T'\to T$ over $B$ is fully faithful on locally constant $\mathbb D$-coefficients, then the pullback $w:E\times_BT'\to E\times_BT$ is a constant-coefficient $\mathbb D$-equivalence. If the same direct-image and base-change hypothesis is required for every locally constant coefficient on every base-changed total category, then the resulting cohomological-fibration class is closed under composition and pullback. The corresponding statements for left Kan extensions and homology follow by duality.

statement: Finite products and the one-fibrant-leg pullback comparison. Assume the hypotheses of A.11 and slice replacement equivalences as in A.12. In the localized fibrant slice over $S$, the product of $X\to S$ and $Y\to S$ is represented by $X\times_S Y\to S$. Arbitrary derived reindexing preserves these finite products. Moreover, if $X\to S$ is intrinsic and $Y\to\overline Y\to S$ is a replacement with $Y\to\overline Y\in W$ and $\overline Y\to S$ intrinsic, then $X\times_S Y\to X\times_S\overline Y$ lies in $W$. statement: The variance assertions of XIII section 4 are lifting adjunctions. Let $\mathcal M(I)=\operatorname{Fun}(I^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal M)$, suppose the ordinary Kan extensions used below exist, and let the two closed lifting pairs be $(C(I),TF(I))$ and $(TC(I),F(I))$, with $C(I),TC(I)$ defined objectwise. For $u:I'\to I$ one has \[ u^*C(I)\subseteq C(I'),\quad u^*TC(I)\subseteq TC(I'), \quad u_*F(I')\subseteq F(I),\quad u_*TF(I')\subseteq TF(I), \] and \[ \begin{split} u^*F(I)\subseteq F(I')&\Longleftrightarrow u_!TC(I')\subseteq TC(I),\\ u^*TF(I)\subseteq TF(I')&\Longleftrightarrow u_!C(I')\subseteq C(I). \end{split} \] If every component of $i\backslash I'$ has an initial object and the relevant coproducts exist, then all four containments in the last two equivalences hold. In particular injective fibrant diagrams are objectwise fibrant. For a walking-arrow diagram $X_0\leftarrow X_1$, injective fibrancy is equivalent to $X_0$ fibrant and $X_1\to X_0\in F$; this also implies that $X_1$ is fibrant.

statement: Closedness upgrades historical exactness to both trivial-class equalities. Let $(C,TC,F,TF)$ satisfy the weak Quillen axioms of XIII ms.~27--28, including two-out-of-three for $W$, the two factorizations, and $TC\subseteq C\cap W$, $TF\subseteq F\cap W$. statement: The uniform theorem of XIII and the exact admissibility hypothesis. statement: A recognition theorem giving all three Kan functors. statement: The genus-zero category and its geometric coefficients. For $n\geq3$, let $\Gamma_n$ be the pure orientation-preserving mapping class group of the $n$-punctured sphere. Set $T_{0,n}=\mathcal C_n^{\op}$. The exit category of $\overline{\mathcal M}_{0,n}(\mathbb C)$ with its dual-tree stratification is $N\mathcal C_n$. For every compactly generated presentable infinity-category $\mathcal V$, \[ \Shv_{\mathrm{cbl}}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{0,n}(\mathbb C);\mathcal V) \simeq\Fun(N\mathcal C_n,\mathcal V) =\Fun(NT_{0,n}^{\op},\mathcal V). \] Forgetting the last mark induces $Q:\mathcal C_{n+1}\to\mathcal C_n$, $\sigma\mapsto q\sigma$, $[g]\mapsto[\phi(g)]$, and $F=Q^{\op}:T_{0,n+1}\to T_{0,n}$. Here $q$ erases curves which become peripheral and identifies repeated isotopy classes, and $\phi:\Gamma_{n+1}\twoheadrightarrow\Gamma_n$ is the forgetful homomorphism.

statement: The exact canonical equivalence criterion for finite posets. For a finite poset $P$ define the colimit-preserving transform \[ (V_PF)(s)= \lim_{t\in P^{\mathrm{op}}} \bigl(\Sigma^\infty_+\operatorname{Hom}_P(t,s)\otimes F(t)\bigr), \qquad V_P:\mathbb D(P)\longrightarrow\mathbb D(P^{\mathrm{op}}). \tag{G.9a} \] There is always a canonical formula \[ p_*^P\simeq p_!^{P^{\mathrm{op}}}V_P. \tag{G.9b} \] For spectra the transform (G.9a) is an equivalence if and only if each strict upper interval $P_{>p}$ is Gorenstein* over $\mathbb Z$. Here a finite poset $L$ is Gorenstein* when every open interval in $L$ with a newly adjoined bottom and top has the integral homology of a sphere; the empty interval is allowed as the $(-1)$-sphere.
